_README: GROUND TRUTH for the Track 5 extraction bench. s97.
EVERY label below was assigned by READING THE SURROUNDING CONTEXT of the cached page,
never by grepping for a number and never by copying the DB record. Those two shortcuts
are what produced FOUR wrong labels in the s96 bench, each of which penalised a model
for being correct.
The DB value is a HINT, NOT A LABEL. A facility's recorded capacity often comes from a
DIFFERENT source than the page under test -- apple-maiden-nc's cited page is Apple's $500B
US-investment release and never mentions Maiden at all, yet the record carries acreage,
utility and on-site generation. Labeling from the DB would score that page as three misses.
FIELDS
capacityAny         - any site-level electrical capacity stated for THIS facility
capacityPlanned     - a planned/designed/entitled/future capacity for THIS facility
capacityOperational - a built/current/in-service capacity for THIS facility
onSiteGenerationMw  - on-site/behind-the-meter generation capacity for THIS facility
VALUES
<number>  the page states this, for this facility
null      the page does not state it (correct answer is abstention)
"AMBIG"   the page states a figure but genuinely does not resolve the distinction;
EXCLUDED from scoring and reported separately. Marking these honestly is
better than inventing a label -- and the AMBIG count is itself a finding:
it measures how often a source even supports the planned/operational split.
accept[]  set of defensible values (e.g. a stated RANGE); any member scores correct.
COOLING TYPE (added 2026-09-01, s121). coolingType is an ENUM field, scored against the
vocabulary in fields.mjs and the decision rule in docs/methodology.md#cooling-type +
lib/schema.ts (waterSchema). All 69 cached pages carry a coolingType label; the 24
non-null ones each quote the sentence they were read from, verified verbatim against
pages.json.
<value>   the page states, FOR THIS FACILITY, a mechanism that the methodology rule
maps to exactly one of evaporative/hybrid/closed_loop/air.
null      the page does not state a mechanism for this facility. This deliberately
INCLUDES water-use volumes ('billions of gallons for cooling'), bare
redundancy or density specs ('Cooling N+1'), site navigation, company-wide
statements, crypto-mining RIG cooling, and IT-side liquid-vs-air delivery.
None of those identify a heat-rejection method, so the pipeline must write
nothing -- prefer a gap to a fabrication.
"AMBIG"   the page says something about THIS facility's cooling that two values could
each defensibly claim, or says only what the design is NOT. 5 of 69.
"unknown" is a real value in the Zod enum but is NEVER a label here. In the dataset it
records a CURATOR's assessment that a source discussed cooling without identifying the
method; an extractor writing it from a passing mention would be manufacturing that
assessment. A model answering "unknown" on a null-labeled page therefore scores as a
hallucination, on purpose.
The DB-value-is-a-hint rule bites hard here. Targets were selected for BALANCE using
the DB's water.coolingType, but the cached page frequently comes from a different
source than the curated value: of 8 facilities the DB records as `hybrid`, ZERO pages
state hybrid, so this corpus cannot measure that value at all. Three labels also
disagree with the DB and are re-curation candidates for a human: edgecore-mesa-az
(DB air -> page says closed_loop), h5-la-vista-ne (DB hybrid -> page says cooling
towers), beltline-luther-horizon-technology-park-ok and global-ai-windsor-co (DB
unknown -> both pages state closed-loop).
AI CLASSIFICATION (added 2026-09-12, s152). aiClassification is an ENUM field, scored
against the vocabulary in fields.mjs and the decision rule in
docs/methodology.md#ai-classification. All 69 cached pages carry a label.
<value>   the page states, FOR THIS FACILITY, something the methodology rule maps to
exactly one of confirmed/likely/mixed_use.
null      the page does not tie this facility to AI. This deliberately INCLUDES
capability marketing ('AI-ready', 'built for the AI era'), an operator's
portfolio-level AI positioning, a sibling site's GPU deployment, and general
industry context ("AI is driving data center demand"). None of those state
anything about THIS facility, so the pipeline must write nothing.
"AMBIG"   the page ties this facility to AI in a way two labels could each defensibly
claim. Excluded from scoring and reported separately.
⚠ The vocabulary has NO member meaning 'assessed, and not AI'. Every member asserts some
degree of AI use, so `null` here means 'the page does not tie this facility to AI' and is
NOT the claim 'this facility is not AI'. A model answering any vocabulary member on a
null-labeled page therefore scores as a hallucination, on purpose — the same convention
coolingType uses for "unknown".
LABEL PROVENANCE, stated plainly because it bounds what these numbers are worth: these
labels were assigned by reading each cached page's text against the methodology rule, in
one pass, with the DB's own aiClassification value WITHHELD from the labeller so it could
not anchor the label (the DB-value-is-a-hint rule above, enforced mechanically this time
rather than by instruction). They are single-pass and have not been double-labelled, so
inter-annotator agreement is unmeasured. Every model/label disagreement was re-read before
being recorded as a model error — that adjudication pass is the only second opinion these
labels have had. Read a disagreement as a possible label bug first.
AI CLASSIFICATION, TWO-VALUE VARIANT (added 2026-09-12, s152). `aiClassificationStated`
is the SAME task as `aiClassification` with the `likely` tier removed: vocabulary is
confirmed | mixed_use only. Its labels are DERIVED MECHANICALLY from the aiClassification
labels above (confirmed->confirmed, mixed_use->mixed_use, null->null, AMBIG->AMBIG) and
introduce no new judgement.
⚠️ The four pages whose aiClassification label is `likely` carry NO aiClassificationStated
key AT ALL. This is deliberate. Their correct answer is not expressible in a two-value
vocabulary, so mapping them to null would score a model CORRECT for abstaining on a page
that genuinely does tie the facility to AI — inventing a label to fill a hole. Omitting the
key makes run.mjs skip the cell and rescore.mjs report it under 'UNLABELED (not scored, NOT
measured)' by name. 63 cells are scorable; 4 omitted, 2 AMBIG-excluded.
This variant exists because the three-value run put 7 of its 8 hallucinations on `likely`.
It tests whether deleting that tier removes those errors or merely relocates them onto
`confirmed`.
